Purpose: To let any component contribute a block to the proposer's prompt, while one assembler keeps the
Caller and time: The prompt assembler of the pass loop, before every pass.
Inputs: `blocks`: the context of the pass (phase, phase attempt, pass ordinal, strategy, what changed
Outputs: Blocks, each with: id, bytes, hash, its writer, `protected` or not, `stable` or `volatile`.
Errors: None of its own. A block over the size its provider declared is cut and recorded.
Guarantees of the core: One assembler budgets the whole prompt, places stable blocks first and keeps the start of the
prompt byte-stable inside a phase attempt. Every pass emits `prompt.built` with the blocks and
what was dropped. A protected block is never dropped. The critic has an assembler and a block set
of its own; no block of the proposer reaches the critic through this point. With the as-is block
set selected, the prompt equals the baseline's byte for byte.
Guarantees of an implementation: A provider is a pure function of the context of the pass and of files it names. It frames text
from outside the runtime as data. It reveals nothing to the proposer about groups, workers or
routing beyond what its content owner specifies.
Failure of an implementation: The block is left out, the omission is recorded in `prompt.built`, and the pass runs. A provider
of a protected block that fails is an error of the pass, by the existing breakers.
Unknown-value rule: An unknown block id is accepted, since block ids are an open set. An unknown value of `protected`
or of `stable` is read as not protected and volatile.
Wave 1 implementations: Spec context; the obligations index; the handoff; feedback; hint; acceleration note; the yield
interface block; the protocol block of the layer `micro`; the reserved-tasks block and the worker
block of the layer `parallel`; the section of the plugin protocol of one harness.
